trigger: ContainerManager scans and picks an empty container as a candidate; its deleteContainer request is posted late (a delay in postDeleteRequest standing in for pacing, GC or a queue backlog). Meanwhile the client deletes the container and re-creates the same path as a PERSISTENT node with data.
reason: ContainerManager.checkContainers builds deleteContainer requests from a candidate list computed earlier and paced over time (ContainerManager.java:140-159). When the request is processed, PrepRequestProcessor checks only childCount==0 and that the node is not a session ephemeral (PrepRequestProcessor.java:326-338). It never checks that the node is still a container or TTL node, or that it is the same node (czxid). The stale request therefore deletes the user's new PERSISTENT node, and the client's later getData on a node it never deleted fails at FinalRequestProcessor.java:673-674. This is silent loss of user data caused by a server-initiated request.
summary: A stale ContainerManager deleteContainer request deletes a PERSISTENT node re-created at the same path, because deleteContainer does not re-check that the target is still a container or TTL node.
